title: Office-Like Application Spawning A Command Interpreter
detection_hypothesis: If macro or template content executes, the interpreter process will retain the document application as its parent image.

field_semantics.ParentImage: Absolute path of the executable that created the process.
field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Low in most environments; noticeable in finance teams with macro workflows.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches are usually repeatable, tied to a specific document path or add-in, and executed by a small set of business users. Tune with the child command line and the invoking document rather than removing the parent process.
tuning_guidance: Add narrow CommandLine exclusions for the exact automation script path. Never exclude an entire office parent image, because that disables the rule for all documents on the endpoint.
test_strategy: Positive cases pair each office-like parent with a different interpreter child. Negative cases keep one half of the pair benign so that both selections are exercised independently.

attack_techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
